# PerfWindow

> PerfWindow is a free, open-source (MIT) Windows hardware monitor by Luka Stojiljković. It shows real-time usage, temperatures, clocks, power and SMART drive health for the CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, motherboard, fans, voltages, battery and network in one dashboard, built on LibreHardwareMonitor. Nothing stays running while it's closed: no tray icon, no startup entry.

Key facts:

- CPU: load per core, package and core temperatures, clocks, Vcore, RAPL power and headroom to TjMax, with Intel P-cores and E-cores shown apart.
- GPU: discrete NVIDIA and AMD cards and Intel integrated graphics, with hot spot and memory junction temperatures, clocks, encoder load, fan, power and VRAM.
- Memory and storage: per-module DIMM temperatures where reported, drive temperatures against each drive's own limits, and SMART lifetime (power-on hours, NVMe wear, data written).
- Six themes (Amber Mainframe, Cyber Slate, Phosphor Tactical, Synthwave Neon, Crimson Terminal and Light) that can follow Windows' light and dark setting. Refresh every 0.5, 1, 2 or 5 seconds, in °C or °F.
- Command line (new in 2.1): `perfwindow-cli` opens a live terminal dashboard of the same readings in the user's theme; piped or run by a script or an AI agent it prints a plain ASCII report, one `Label: value` reading per line, or JSON with `--json`. It is off until turned on in Settings → Command line.
- Architecture: a Rust and egui dashboard that runs as the user, and a .NET sensor service running as LocalSystem that starts on demand (one UAC prompt per launch) and exits when the dashboard closes. They talk over a named pipe.
- The installer adds the signed PawnIO driver for CPU temperature, clock and power registers, and the Visual C++ runtime when missing.
- Reads sensors only: no overclocking, undervolting or fan control. No telemetry; the only network request is an optional, anonymous update check against GitHub at most once every six hours.
- Requires Windows 11, or Windows 10 version 1607 or later, x64.

## Reading the sensors from an agent

On a Windows machine with PerfWindow 2.1 or later installed and Settings → Command line turned on (which puts `perfwindow-cli` on the user `PATH`):

- `perfwindow-cli --json`: every reading as one JSON object, temperatures in °C. Characters outside ASCII are written as escapes.
- `perfwindow-cli --once`: one plain ASCII report, one `Label: value` reading per line.
- `perfwindow-cli --watch 5 --json`: one JSON object per line every 5 seconds (1 to 60) until stopped.
- Exit codes: 0 success, 2 bad arguments, 3 command-line readings are off in Settings, 4 the sensor service is unavailable or stopped.
- Starting the sensor service needs the user to approve a Windows (UAC) prompt, and the command and the PerfWindow window cannot read the sensors at the same time.
